title: Actionable incident scripts packaged as task libraries + lightweight CLI
creator: Asha Patel
description: Package curated incident remediation steps (safe, reversible operations) as versioned, auditable task packages and expose them through a tiny cross-platform CLI (ops-pack). Goal: reduce MTTR by enabling SREs and oncall to execute vetted procedures safely with dry-run, approval, and telemetry. Focus areas: idempotent steplets, RBAC-scoped execution, audit records in existing logging pipeline, and integration with runbook executor for preflight checks.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: ops-pack can list/install/validate a task package from the internal registry
AC2: CLI supports dry-run and explain modes that emit all API calls without mutating state
AC3: Executions create audit events (user, package-version, args, result) visible in ops-telemetry dashboard
AC4: Task packages are signature-verified and can be marked 'safe' or 'requires-approval'
AC5: End-to-end canary: staging oncall can run a safe package and confirm no regressions
design_decisions: Use a tiny JSON/YAML task package schema (v0.1) with explicit pre/post checks and rollback hooks
Implement the CLI as a single static binary (Go) to reduce runtime deps for paging/mobile usage
Rely on the existing runbook executor for step orchestration; ops-pack will act as a package manager and thin launcher
Enforce RBAC by mapping package actions to internal permission scopes; write operations require 'ops:exec' role
Emit structured telemetry events to the existing diagnostics pipeline so Grafana/Looker can report MTTR improvements
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental destructive ops by junior users -> Mitigation: default packages to dry-run + require explicit --apply flag and optionally two-step approval for high-risk packages
Risk: package tampering -> Mitigation: sign packages with central key and verify signatures in CLI and CI
Risk: permission creep -> Mitigation: scoping rules and LDAP group-based approvals; audit every grant
Risk: increased oncall cognitive load -> Mitigation: limit initial package surface to 8 vetted actions and add decision guidance in each package
